phases.title: Before the move: fix the blockers and make the decisions
phases.intro: Everything here is settled while the account is still at its current position. NO-GO steps block the move; REVIEW steps need a decision or a check by hand.

steps.title: Move the organization Config aggregator larkspur-org-aggregator out of the account first
steps.detail: The aggregator lives in this account; leaving breaks aggregation for the whole source organization. Create the aggregator in the account that stays, confirm it receives data, then delete this one.
steps.finding: Account hosts the organization Config aggregator larkspur-org-aggregator

steps.title: Hand over delegated administration for config.amazonaws.com before the account leaves
steps.detail: Delegated administration is tied to organization membership. Leaving the organization removes the delegation, and the service's organization-wide view (and often its member enrolment) with it. Re-delegate to another account before the move. Some services need the administrator disabled in the service itself first (GuardDuty, Security Hub, Macie, Inspector and Detective have a disable-organization-admin-account call); the organization-wide view of the service moves to the stand-in.
steps.finding: Account is the delegated administrator for config.amazonaws.com

steps.title: Make the account able to stand alone
steps.detail: Before it can leave, the account needs its own contact information, a payment method, a support plan choice and completed identity verification. It then has to be invited by the target management account and accept the invitation. SCPs in the source that deny organizations:LeaveOrganization must be lifted for the move. Contact information, alternate contacts and the payment method can be checked with the Account API; identity verification and the support plan are done in the console.
steps.where: account larkspur-security (111111111113), signed in as root or an administrator
steps.finding: Standalone account prerequisites and invitation
commands: # console: Billing and Cost Management → Payment preferences; Account → Identity verification; Support → Support plan

steps.title: Lift the deny on organizations:LeaveOrganization in SCP Larkspur-Baseline-Guardrails / DenyLeaveOrganization, or let the management account remove the account
steps.detail: SCP Larkspur-Baseline-Guardrails (p-lark0001) is attached at root Root (r-lark) and denies organizations:LeaveOrganization without a condition, so leave-organization run from inside the account fails. Either detach the policy or edit the statement for the duration of the move and put it back afterwards, or run remove-account-from-organization from the management account, which SCPs do not restrict.
steps.finding: Standalone account prerequisites and invitation
commands: aws organizations describe-policy --policy-id p-lark0001 --query Content --output text
aws organizations remove-account-from-organization --account-id 111111111113   # the alternative that needs no policy change

evidence.note: Deny organizations:LeaveOrganization

steps.title: Find what references the 2 AWSReservedSSO_* role(s) of the account
steps.detail: Identity Center deletes the IAM roles it provisioned in the account (path /aws-reserved/sso.amazonaws.com/us-east-1/) when the account leaves the organization. Anything that names these roles breaks: resource and trust policies, KMS key policies, S3 bucket policies, EKS access entries, pipelines and tools that assume them, and CloudTrail history keeps the old ARNs. The target instance provisions new roles with a different random suffix, so references have to be updated, not restored. The exact suffix is only visible in IAM; offline the roles are known by their pattern. List the exact role ARNs now, while they exist, and search for them so the references can be updated after the move.
steps.finding: 2 AWSReservedSSO_* role(s) are deleted from the account: AWSReservedSSO_AdministratorAccess_*, AWSReservedSSO_ReadOnlyAccess_*

phases.title: Before the move: re-create what does not travel
phases.intro: Shares, delegations, permission sets and stacks that are scoped to the account's current position do not follow it. Prepare the replacements now so nothing is interrupted.

steps.title: Re-share larkspur-core-network with the account directly: ec2:Subnet, ec2:TransitGateway, route53resolver:ResolverRule
steps.detail: Owner 111111111112 shares larkspur-core-network (ec2:Subnet, ec2:TransitGateway, route53resolver:ResolverRule) with arn:aws:organizations::111111111111:organization/o-larkspur0001 today. After the move those principals no longer cover the account. Ask the owner to add account 111111111113 as a principal before the move so nothing attached to these resources is interrupted. The account will be outside the organization, so the share has to allow external principals and the account has to accept an invitation. This is a networking share: the move stays NO-GO until it is done.
steps.finding: Networking share larkspur-core-network is lost: ec2:Subnet, ec2:TransitGateway, route53resolver:ResolverRule

steps.title: Enable trusted access in Fernhill Group (o-fernhill0001) for: account.amazonaws.com
steps.detail: Organization-integrated features of these services (for example organization-wide GuardDuty, RAM sharing with the organization, service-managed StackSets) are not available in the target organization until trusted access is enabled there. Only for the integrations the account relies on; enabling trusted access is an organization-wide setting.

steps.detail: Account Factory assumes this role to enroll an existing account. It needs AdministratorAccess and a trust policy for the target management account. Also make sure no Config recorder or delivery channel of the account's own conflicts in the governed regions.

steps.title: Review permission set AdministratorAccess in the target instance before re-assigning it
steps.detail: Account assignments exist only for accounts inside the organization that owns the instance. When the account leaves o-larkspur0001, Identity Center deletes these 1 assignment(s) and the principals lose this access at once. The target instance has a permission set with the same name; re-assign the principals to it once the account has joined. They are matched by name only: identity store d-fern0000001 is a different directory, so the users and groups are different objects there. Same name, different settings: session duration PT1H vs PT2H.

phases.title: The move
phases.intro: Run these in order. Between leaving and accepting the invitation the account is standalone, with no SCPs and no organization features; keep that window short.

steps.title: Invite the account into Fernhill Group (o-fernhill0001)
steps.detail: The invitation (a handshake) is valid for 15 days. Send it before the account leaves so the standalone window is short.
commands: aws organizations invite-account-to-organization --target Id=111111111113,Type=ACCOUNT --notes "Move of larkspur-security planned with orgshift"

steps.title: Leave Larkspur Holdings (o-larkspur0001)
steps.detail: Run leave-organization from inside the account, or remove it from the management account (which SCPs do not restrict). Both need the standalone prerequisites to be in place. From this moment no SCP, RCP or tag policy of the source applies, organization-scoped shares stop reaching the account and Identity Center deletes its assignments and roles.
steps.where: account larkspur-security (111111111113), or management account 111111111111 of Larkspur Holdings
commands: aws organizations leave-organization   # run inside the account
aws organizations remove-account-from-organization --account-id 111111111113   # alternative, run by the management account

steps.title: Accept the invitation
steps.detail: The account joins Fernhill Group (o-fernhill0001) at its root with the AWS managed default policies attached. Everything on the verdict board that applies at the target position applies from the next step on.
commands: aws organizations accept-handshake --handshake-id <handshake ID from the previous command>

steps.title: Move the account from the root to OU Core (ou-fern-core)
steps.detail: Until this call the account sits at the target root with only the policies attached there.

phases.title: After the move: checks
phases.intro: Confirm what the simulation predicted and finish what could only be done once the account is at its new position.

steps.title: Confirm the account sits under OU Core (ou-fern-core) and the expected policies reach it
steps.detail: The parent must be ou-fern-core. The policies listed for the account should match the target chain of the simulation (added: SCP Fernhill-Root-Guardrails, SCP aws-guardrails-ztmvqe, TAG Fernhill-Cost-Allocation).

Each administrator's auto-enable settings decide whether the account is enrolled on joining; check the service consoles for the new member.

Preventive controls apply through the OU's SCPs at once; detective and proactive ones report once the account is enrolled.

steps.title: Enroll the account in Control Tower from Account Factory (OU Core)
steps.detail: Moving into a registered OU does not enroll the account by itself. The 1 preventive guardrail SCP(s) on the OU chain apply immediately because they are attached to the OUs, but the 1 detective control(s) do not report and the baseline is not deployed until the account is enrolled from Account Factory. Enrolment needs an AWSControlTowerExecution role in the account that trusts management account 222222222221, no conflicting Config recorder or delivery channel in the governed regions (eu-west-1, eu-central-1), and an email address and name that Account Factory can register. The account has to have joined o-fernhill0001 before it can be enrolled.
steps.where: management account 222222222221 of Fernhill Group (Account Factory)
